text: How should SkyHarbor compare Loyalty AI and IROPS AI as investment choices?
claudePromptBoundary: Full production prompt is reconstructed from current source template and captured source packet. ai_egress_audit stores prompt hash/snapshot refs, not raw prompt text by default.
claudeResponse:
Airline Demo should treat these as two different investment classes, not two horses in the same race. Loyalty AI is a revenue-lift bet with a partially proven value line and adjacent-risk controls; IROPS AI is an operational-resilience bet where the value is larger and more strategic, but readiness gates dominate the near-term ROI. My
fund Loyalty AI to scale on its existing proof, and fund IROPS AI as a readiness program first, autonomous scale second. 9M target value, sponsor is CFO, RAG is Amber, and the "AI value proof" KPI in the Loyalty and Co-brand area is tracking usable.
That's the profile of a bet you double down on: sponsor alignment, value proof underway, contained blast radius (member offers, co-brand economics, engagement). 9M target is Finance-approved realized value or planning-grade.
On IROPS AI, the value pool is larger — recovery decisions touch aircraft, crew legality, passenger reaccommodation, turns, maintenance, and disruption comms — but the readiness spine is not there yet.
The loaded CTO packet flags open gates on finance-approved disruption-cost baseline, certified data freshness for crew legality and PNR/flight-status feeds, model-risk tiering, HITL workflow, and vendor SLA linkage. IROPS recovery decisioning is explicitly tagged early-stage AI maturity in the capability inventory. Investing in autonomous IROPS scale before those gates close is where airline peers stall.
The decision
Loyalty AI is a scale-and-measure bet this fiscal year; IROPS AI is a sequence-foundations bet where the first tranche funds the IROPS Data Foundation, Operational Event Streaming, Crew Recovery Modernization, and AI Governance Readiness programs — not the autonomous recovery agent. Compare them on value class and gate posture, not on headline ROI.
9M target as realized vs. planning value, and Finance-approved disruption-cost baseline by event category for IROPS. Want me to sketch the gate-to-value roadmap for IROPS, or pressure-test the Loyalty scale case first?
